title: The Hollow Archive
premise: Coral Hartwell has spent nine years alone on Kepler Station, tending a seed vault garden and a beacon whose original orders were scrubbed from every database. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with its crew biologically reversed into children, Coral realizes her forgotten beacon was the last thing to record what happened to them—and someone is erasing that record in real time. As corporate auditors arrive to certify the station for decommission, Coral races to recover corrupted logs, uncovering that the 'massacre' was a deliberate cull of the Meridian's colonists to hide a discovery about the terraforming project itself. In the end, Coral broadcasts the truth on the beacon she was always meant to tend, sacrificing her invisibility and her claim to the only home she's known, but gaining the family she never expected: the Meridian's children, who remember her voice from the beacon's lullabies.
about_author: Xanthe Halloran is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent a decade designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction. Their work explores the quiet violence of systems that forget the people who maintain them.

chapters.title: Seed Inventory
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She tends the vault garden on Kepler Station, cataloguing seeds for colonists who may never come, and performs her daily ritual: checking a beacon she can't explain and can't abandon. The chapter establishes her isolation and the small comfort of routine. Beat: contentment shadowed by an unnameable wrongness.

chapters.title: The Beacon Answers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The beacon, silent for nine years, transmits a handshake protocol to an incoming vessel—the Meridian, presumed lost decades ago. Coral realizes the ship has been answering her beacon's automated calls. She scrambles to prepare docking for a crew that should be adults. Beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with interludes from the Meridian's logs. The ship docks; aboard are twenty-three children with adult memories flickering behind young eyes. Their captain, now a girl of nine, recognizes Coral's beacon signal and calls her by name. Beat: horror and tenderness entwined.

chapters.title: Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Medical scans confirm the impossible: the crew is biologically de-aging, their memories degrading in reverse order—the oldest memories first. The children are forgetting their mission, their families, themselves. Coral becomes their reluctant caretaker. Beat: grief for people still alive.

chapters.title: What the Logs Don't Say
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The Meridian's black box is wiped; the station's own records show the Meridian never launched. Coral finds a fragment: her beacon recorded an emergency broadcast the night the ship vanished—a massacre signal, since scrubbed. Beat: the first proof that erasure is deliberate.

chapters.title: The Auditor
chapters.summary: New POV: Idris Vane, a TerraForm Solutions auditor, arrives to certify Kepler Station for decommission. Charming and thorough, he asks oddly precise questions about the beacon's transmission history. Coral hides the children. Beat: a predator wearing a bureaucrat's face.

chapters.title: Twenty-Three Small Witnesses
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and the eldest child, Sef (mentally a forty-year-old navigator in a nine-year-old body). Sef remembers fragments of the cull: adults turning on each other after finding something in the deep survey data. Beat: the children are evidence, and evidence gets destroyed.

chapters.title: Gardens for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, quieter chapter. She teaches the children to tend the vault garden; the work grounds their fracturing memories. Sef tells her the Meridian's mission was never terraforming—it was a retrieval. Beat: belonging blooming in the wrong place at the wrong time.

chapters.title: Commissioned by Nobody
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She digs into the station's founding records and finds her own employment file forged nine years ago—she was placed here to maintain the beacon by someone who knew the Meridian would return. Beat: her entire identity was a cover story, and she never knew.

chapters.title: Vane's Inventory
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Vane finds traces of the children—a second ration draw, small footprints in the hydroponics bay. He files a quiet report and requests an enforcement detail, revealing to the reader that the cull order is still active. Beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: The Lullaby Frequency
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She discovers why the children trust her: the beacon has broadcast a coded lullaby every night for nine years—a reassurance signal aimed at the Meridian's flight path. Someone programmed it to keep the crew calm through whatever was coming. Beat: she was their guardian before they ever met.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, memories surfacing. The Meridian found an artifact in deep space: evidence that the terraforming program's target worlds were already inhabited—by humans, seeded long ago. The company's founding mythology collapsed, so the crew had to. Beat: the massacre had a motive, and it was existential.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vane presents the certification: Kepler Station will be scuttled in six days, crew and cargo 'disposed per protocol.' Coral signs under duress, buying time, and begins planning. Beat: cold fear converted to resolve.

chapters.title: Corrupted on Purpose
chapters.summary: Coral and Sef's POV, alternating. They reconstruct the beacon's raw buffer, finding the massacre broadcast fragmented but recoverable—except the final segment, which requires the Meridian's physical flight recorder, still sealed in the ship's reversed and failing systems. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Children Forget
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The youngest children lose language; Sef begins losing his navigation memories, forgetting the coordinates that prove where the artifact was found. Coral records everything—their voices, their stories—as both archive and act of love. Beat: racing against forgetting itself.

chapters.title: What Coral Was For
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She decodes the forged employment trail and finds her handler: a company founder who seeded beacons across the frontier as dead-man switches against exactly this cover-up. Coral was never an accident; she was the failsafe. Beat: fury and strange relief—her loneliness had a purpose.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Idris's POV turning sympathetic. Vane's enforcement detail arrives early; reviewing Coral's file, he realizes the 'disposal protocol' includes him—he was hired to be a witness who wouldn't survive certification. He defects, bringing access codes. Beat: the instrument of erasure choosing memory.

chapters.title: The Flight Recorder
chapters.summary: Coral, Sef, and Vane raid the Meridian's sealed core while enforcement sweeps the station. The ship, half-reversed, fights them—automated defenses still obeying the cull order. Sef, running on muscle memory older than his body, navigates them through. Beat: sacrifice and competence under fire.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Coral's POV. With enforcement breaching the garden, she keys the beacon to transmit the recovered massacre record, the artifact coordinates, and the children's testimony to every colony relay in range. The station's power dies mid-broadcast; she finishes it by hand, burning out the beacon she tended for nine years. Beat: the invisible woman making herself unmistakable.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The broadcast propagates; colony relays echo it faster than the company can scrub. Enforcement stands down as their own crews receive the record. Vane opens the station's doors to the incoming response ships. Beat: exhale after the held breath.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The company collapses into inquiry; the children are promised homes, but homes mean separation. Coral has no legal identity—her file was forged, her station decommissioned. Sef, now forgetting her name, still hums the lullaby. Beat: victory that costs the victor her place in the world.

chapters.title: New Commission
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. The colony council offers her something no one forged: a real contract, a real garden, and guardianship of the Meridian's children, who vote unanimously to stay with 'the beacon lady.' She plants the first seed of a garden meant for people finally born. Beat: belonging, earned and chosen.
